bio:
I am a full-stack engineer at Hybrid Interactive Consultancy in Kochi. Most of my work is line-of-business software: CRM, ERP, hospital and HR systems that a company's daily operations depend on. That means the hard parts are rarely the framework. They are the tenancy model, the audit trail, the state machine that decides what a document can become next, and whether the person after me can still read the code.

I work mostly in FastAPI and Next.js, on a modular monolith pattern with async SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, Redis and Celery behind it. Alongside the client work I put together two of the standards our new projects start from: a Next.js frontend template, and a backend conventions kit that collects the rules we learned the expensive way.
principles: Write for the person debugging this at 2am, not for the person reading it today.
A document that lies is worse than no document. Date it, or delete it.
Decide the tenancy, audit and permission model on day one. All three get expensive in month six.
AI tooling raises how much you ship. It does not lower the bar for what you ship.
